lessonTitle: Why Do We Protect National Parks?
title: Full of Life

badge.name: Ranger Star
badge.line: Only VR crews earn this one. Your shot goes in Opti's film.

hook.look: This is a filming permit. A permit says you are allowed to do something.
hook.head: Scene 25 · Full of Life
hook.alt: Many white wading birds feeding together in shallow water and tall grass
hook.cap: Wading birds feed together at Shark Valley in Everglades National Park, Florida.
hook.note: This park was set aside in 1947 to keep its wildlife safe. Why does it need so many kinds of life?

opti.brief: Welcome to the park, crew. We film Scene 25, Full of Life. Show me why a park needs many kinds of life, then take the shot.

steps.title: Know your models
steps.html:
Type each gray word in the Filter models box.

@MODELS@

This list is also on the Canvas tab in VR.

steps.title: Go on location
steps.html:
🔗 First time only: connect Canvas at xr.optimaed.com. See Having trouble in VR? below.

Open the On-Demand app. Click Explore. Type Medieval in Filter environments. Click Medieval Forest, then Begin Solo.

steps.title: Build the scene
steps.html:
Press the top button on your right controller, then click Models. Put the Panther and the Deer under the trees. Set the Owl, the Frog and the Bromeliad near them.

✋ Grab a model with the palm trigger. Use both palm triggers to make it bigger or smaller.
🗣 Say it out loud: “This park protects many kinds of life. The ___ needs the ___ because ___.”

steps.title: Take the shot and send it
steps.html:
Stand back so the whole scene fits. Open your menu, click Library, then Camera. Click Take photo.

Click the Canvas tab and pick @CANVAS@. Click Choose from My Files, pick your photo, click Use this file, then Submit to Canvas. Look for the green Submitted tag.

🔁 Want to fix it? Move the models, take a new photo and send it again.

steps.title: Check and leave
steps.html: Press the Meta button, then click Quit. Check that your photo is in the Canvas assignment. Not there? Open Having trouble in VR?

extra.html: Add one more living thing the park protects: Monarch Butterfly

vr.full: Your photo shows the Panther, the Deer, the Owl, the Frog and the Bromeliad together in the forest.

studio.title: Wire the food web

labels.start: Tap an animal. Then tap what it eats.
labels.pick: {from} is picked. Now tap what it eats.
labels.snipStart: Now tap the scissors to snip the grasshoppers.
labels.snipFirst: Tap the scissors first, or drag them onto the grasshopper.
labels.done: You pinned the web, snipped it and made your claim. Nice work, crew!

studio.look: A food web is a map of who eats whom. Here it is a string board, like a film crew uses. Each card is a real photo from Florida. A species is one kind of living thing.
studio.do: Tap an animal, then tap what it eats. A red string joins them. You can also drag one card onto the other. Then snip one species and see who has a harder time.

claim.name: My claim
claim.alt: Many white wading birds feeding together in shallow water and tall grass
claim.q: Which place can lose one species and stay healthy?

options.many: 🌿 A park with many kinds of living things.
options.one: 🌾 A field with only one kind of plant.

claim.miss: Think about the web. More kinds of food means more ways to find a meal.

frames.lead: 1. Why does a park need many kinds of life?
frames.starter: I think a park needs many kinds of living things because ___.

frames.lead: 2. What did the snip show you?
frames.starter: When the grasshoppers were gone, ___, so ___.

studio.full: You pinned all 6 strings, found who lost food and picked the claim. Your 2 sentences have at least 20 words.

species.name: Egret
species.alt: Great egret, a tall white bird, wading among cypress trees
species.food: An egret eats frogs, fish and big bugs. Try again.

species.name: Panther
species.alt: Florida panther walking through a green forest
species.food: A panther hunts big animals, like deer. Try again.

species.name: Frog
species.alt: Green frog sitting in shallow water
species.food: A frog eats bugs. Try again.

species.name: Deer
species.alt: White-tailed deer standing in tall grass
species.food: A deer eats plants. Try again.

species.name: Grasshopper
species.alt: Yellow and black lubber grasshopper on a gray stone
species.food: A grasshopper eats plants. Try again.

species.name: Sawgrass
species.alt: Tall sawgrass with brown flower heads under a blue sky
species.food: Sawgrass is a plant. It makes its own food from sunlight. Tap an animal first.

links.msg: String pinned! A grasshopper eats grass.
String pinned! A deer eats grass and other plants.
String pinned! A frog eats grasshoppers.
String pinned! An egret eats frogs.
String pinned! An egret eats grasshoppers too.
String pinned! A panther hunts deer.

web.name: The food web
web.alt: Tall sawgrass with brown flower heads under a blue sky
web.done: All 6 strings are pinned. That is a food web! Now snip one species.

snip.name: The snip
snip.alt: Yellow and black lubber grasshopper on a gray stone
snip.q: The grasshoppers are gone. Tap every animal that has a harder time finding food.

ok.frog: Yes. The frog lost a food. Frogs eat other bugs too, so it can still find some.
ok.egret: Yes. The egret lost grasshoppers. It still has frogs and fish to eat.

safe.deer: The deer eats plants, not grasshoppers. The deer is OK.
safe.panther: The panther eats deer. The deer are OK, so the panther is OK.
safe.grass: Sawgrass is a plant. With no grasshoppers, less of it gets eaten.

snip.done: Two animals lost a food, but they have other foods. Many kinds of life keep a park going.
